headline: ASX finished strong today while last night's NASDAQ tumbled 2.15% — US tech dragged your GOOG and MSFT lower, but your local ETFs held up well.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Best mover on the ASX today, up 3.15%. The AI sector got a local boost as the ASX followed through on positive sentiment — even as US tech wobbled last night, Aussie AI-themed stocks had a strong session.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Fell $10.39 last night as the broader NASDAQ sold off hard. No company-specific bad news — it was a market-wide tech pullback. Long-term story remains intact with Microsoft one of Wall Street's top AI earnings plays heading into reporting season.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Dropped nearly 2% last night alongside the broader NASDAQ tech selloff. The fundamentals story hasn't changed — Citi still holds a $270 price target ahead of GTA VI, and analysts are now floating the possibility of a new Red Dead Redemption title in 2027-28 as an additional catalyst.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Biggest mover in the portfolio last night, down 2.32% as NASDAQ dropped sharply. The selling appears to be market-wide rather than Google-specific — a Motley Fool analyst is actually predicting Google Cloud revenue could exceed 100% growth when Alphabet reports earnings on October 28.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Up just under 1% today on the ASX. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, and today's local price gain reflects AUD pricing adjustments — the underlying US market actually fell last night.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Solid session today, up 0.99%. As a diversified multi-asset ETF it absorbed last night's US tech weakness across a broad basket of global shares — exactly what diversification is supposed to do.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: Quiet but positive day, up 0.89% as the ASX broadly rallied. This is a 100% growth-focused diversified ETF — it tracks closely with global equity markets and had a solid session.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Modest gain today on the ASX. Emerging markets have been steadier than developed markets amid Middle East tensions and rising oil prices, which can benefit some emerging-market exporters.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Barely moved today, up just 0.34%. There's fresh headwind news — lithium prices reportedly dropped 14% after an EU-China hybrid car deal was announced that could reduce long-term battery demand. The stock is already well down from where you bought in, so today's tiny gain is cold comfort.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings on October 28 — big moment approaching
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings in 10 days. A Motley Fool analyst is predicting Google Cloud revenue growth could exceed 100% — which would be a massive beat. Last night's price dip (-2.32%) looks like general market noise rather than anything Google-specific. If Cloud delivers, this could be a strong catalyst. As a long-term holder, sit tight and watch the October 28 result.

watch_today.title: PLS: Lithium headwinds are real and deepening
watch_today.detail: New data shows lithium prices fell 14% after the EU and China struck a hybrid car deal that reduces the projected demand for lithium batteries. Pilbara is already down 55.8% from your entry price. The structural demand story for lithium hasn't completely collapsed, but this is a genuine setback — not just short-term noise. Worth watching closely as the EV transition timeline gets messier.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold steady through the tech selloff
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell nearly 2% last night but there's zero company-specific bad news. It's a Wall Street darling for AI earnings and Motley Fool analysts are bullish on where the stock sits by 2030. For a long-term holder, a rough night on the NASDAQ is not a reason to move. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Citi holds $270 target, GTA VI still the big catalyst
watch_today.detail: Take-Two slipped nearly 2% last night in the broader selloff, but Citi is maintaining its $270 price target ahead of GTA VI — well above the current $205. There's also analyst chatter about a new Red Dead Redemption title arriving 2027-28. You're currently down 4.9% on this position but the long-term gaming thesis remains intact. Hold.

watch_today.title: Oil nudging $99 — watch for inflation and rate implications
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil rose another 1% last night to nearly $99/barrel. With Middle East tensions running hot (UAE and Saudi re-entering Yemen, ongoing Iran-Israel conflict), oil near $100 could keep inflation sticky globally — which means central banks including the RBA may stay cautious about cutting rates. Worth watching for knock-on effects on your bond-heavy ETFs.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision watch — unemployment rising
watch_today.detail: Australian unemployment figures are rising and markets are eyeing the RBA for any hints on the rate outlook. If the RBA signals rates may come down sooner, that's generally good for growth assets across your portfolio. No decision imminent but the data is shifting in a direction that could benefit long-term investors.

world.summary: A deadly incident and major fire at a Canadian military base dominated global headlines today, while the Middle East conflict escalated with UAE and Saudi Arabia re-entering Yemen and oil pushing toward $100. US midterm politics is heating up with Trump under pressure.

stories.title: Deaths and major fire at Canadian military base in Alberta
stories.why_it_matters: A serious incident at a Canadian Forces military base in Alberta has resulted in confirmed deaths and injuries, triggering a major fire that spread beyond the base perimeter. Details are still emerging but it's being treated as a significant national security event. Multiple international outlets including Reuters, NPR and the Irish Independent are covering it. Canada has put emergency services on high alert in the region.

stories.title: UAE and Saudi Arabia agree to re-enter the Yemen conflict as Houthis gain ground
stories.why_it_matters: The UAE and Saudi Arabia have struck a deal to re-engage militarily in Yemen after Houthi rebels — backed by Iran — made significant territorial gains. This is a major escalation in one of the world's most devastating conflicts, which has already killed hundreds of thousands of people. It also tightens the link between the Yemen conflict and the broader Iran-US-Israel tensions, raising the risk of a wider regional war.

stories.title: Oil near $99: How the US-Iran war has upended global trade routes
stories.why_it_matters: The conflict between the US and Iran has severely disrupted two of the world's most critical oil shipping routes — the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. About 20% of global oil supply passes through the Strait of Hormuz alone. With crude oil now sitting near $99/barrel, energy costs are rising globally, which feeds into higher inflation everywhere — including Australia's petrol prices and the cost of goods.

stories.title: Trump faults aides as Republican midterm prospects dim ahead of US elections
stories.why_it_matters: With US midterm elections approaching, Trump is publicly blaming his own aides for poor polling numbers and has been reviving 2020 election conspiracy theories. The Guardian reports his Justice Department is also testing the limits of separation of powers — meaning checks and balances between the President and the courts. A bad midterm result for Republicans could shift the balance of Congress and affect Trump's ability to pass legislation, including policies affecting trade and tariffs that flow through to Australian exports.

stories.title: The Strait of Hormuz: A 'violent new normal' threatening global oil supply
stories.why_it_matters: The Independent reports that ongoing military incidents in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow passage between Iran and Oman through which a fifth of the world's oil flows — have created what analysts are calling a 'violent new normal.' Ship attacks, drone strikes and naval standoffs are now frequent rather than exceptional. This sustained instability is a key reason oil prices remain elevated near $99, with real consequences for global inflation and central bank decisions.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid day, closing up 1% to 8,806. Last night was rough for US markets — the NASDAQ dropped 2.15% and the S&P 500 fell 1.09% as tech stocks sold off broadly. Gold edged up slightly and oil is creeping toward $100. The Aussie dollar ticked up to 69.5 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong close today — up 87 points, or 1%. Good session for local shares.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session: fell 84.6 points as tech led the market lower.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night: dropped over 573 points — the big tech names took a real beating.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil is knocking on the door of $100 — Middle East tensions driving the price higher.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold held near record highs — investors staying cautious and using it as a safe haven.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged higher to nearly 69.5 US cents — good for buying imported goods, small drag on unhedged US share returns when converted back to AUD.

politics.summary: Attention is on the RBA as Australian unemployment edges up, with markets watching for any hint of rate cuts. Not much else breaking on the domestic front today.

stories.title: Unemployment rising — all eyes on the RBA for rate hints
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's unemployment numbers are on the rise, and that's shifting market expectations around when the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) might start cutting interest rates. If unemployment keeps climbing, the RBA is under more pressure to ease — cutting rates would lower borrowing costs for mortgages and stimulate spending. For investors, lower rates generally support share prices, especially for growth-oriented assets like ETFs. No RBA meeting imminent but the data is moving in a direction that matters.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the big theme this weekend globally — California's governor is pushing new rules, Anthropic has proposed a safety bill, and the AI chatbot wars are heating up with Google's Gemini 4 Argon now competing with Claude and GPT-6.

stories.title: California Governor Newsom pushes AI regulation — with an eye on 2028 presidential run
stories.why_it_matters: California Governor Gavin Newsom is ramping up AI regulation in his state, positioning himself as a responsible tech governor ahead of a likely 2028 presidential run. California is home to most major AI companies including Google and Anthropic, so state-level rules there effectively become national policy. This is relevant for your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings — more regulation can slow rollouts but also provides the 'guardrails' big companies prefer over a patchwork of rules.

stories.title: Anthropic's AI Safety Bill sets a surprisingly high bar for government action
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI company behind the Claude chatbot and partly backed by Google — has proposed an AI safety bill that critics say sets the threshold for government intervention so high that regulators would rarely be able to act. Mother Jones reports the bill's definition of 'dangerous AI' is so narrow it would only kick in for the most extreme scenarios. This matters because it shapes how much freedom AI companies will have to operate with minimal oversight.

stories.title: The AI chatbot arms race: Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude vs GPT-6
stories.why_it_matters: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now being compared head-to-head with Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-6, with analysts publishing 'which one should you switch to?' guides. The competition in AI chatbots is fierce — for Google, winning this race is critical to maintaining its dominance in search and cloud. As a GOOG holder, how Google's AI performs against rivals like Microsoft's Copilot (powered by OpenAI) directly affects the company's long-term revenue.

stories.title: UK Labour figures are worried about AI — but also scared of being seen as behind the curve
stories.why_it_matters: Senior figures inside the UK's Labour government are privately concerned that AI is advancing faster than policy can keep up — but they're also worried about looking like luddites (anti-technology) if they push too hard for regulation. The Guardian reports this internal tension is creating a policy vacuum in Britain. It mirrors debates happening in Australia and the US: how do you govern something that's changing faster than parliaments can write laws?

sport.summary: Rugby League World Cup action dominated the weekend — Tonga pulled off a massive win over England, Fiji beat Cook Islands, and PNG secured a big result. NRL off-season moves are heating up too.

stories.title: Tonga stun England in historic Rugby League World Cup win
stories.why_it_matters: Tonga have made a massive statement at the Rugby League World Cup, defeating England in what NRL.com is calling a historic result. It's a significant upset that signals the growing depth of Pacific Island rugby league — and huge news for the NRL community in Queensland and across Australia.

stories.title: Fiji's Bati blast Cook Islands in Rugby League World Cup opener
stories.why_it_matters: Fiji's Bati ran in a first-half blitz to take down Cook Islands at the Rugby League World Cup. Fiji rode a strong early momentum to secure the win — a promising start for one of the Pacific's most dangerous teams in the tournament.

stories.title: PNG secure big World Cup win with Cowboys flyer starring
stories.why_it_matters: Papua New Guinea secured a commanding World Cup win, with a Cowboys (NRL's North Queensland Cowboys) flyer putting in a standout individual performance. PNG's rise as a rugby league power is one of the great stories of the sport — and their World Cup campaign is being watched closely across the Pacific.

stories.title: Roosters 19 defeat Knights 18 in NRL Grand Final thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL Premiership with a nail-biting 19-18 win over the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium. One point the margin — it doesn't get tighter than that in a Grand Final.

stories.title: Navratilova slams Australian Open crowd after Djokovic booing: 'It's just disgusting'
stories.why_it_matters: Tennis legend Martina Navratilova publicly blasted the crowd at the Australian Open after sections of the crowd booed Novak Djokovic, calling the behaviour 'just disgusting.' The incident has reignited the debate about how Australian tennis crowds treat certain players — and whether the Open's famously raucous atmosphere has crossed a line.
